The Warrant may assign engineers, troops, protection, and consequences, but it cannot replace chamber sequence or absolve a flood imposed on inhabited ground.
The villages supply canal knowledge and identify the households and fields lying beneath the flood marks outside the embankment.
The Sluice sheet preserves the three-lock sequence, load relationships, work spaces, and low-ground risk without revealing the present water or gate state.
Vossgard contains the Underkeep Gate and gives the canal its competing uses as supply route, assault road, and organized exit.

encounters.title: Vossgard
encounters.summary: Every open road and unsupported promise takes its appointed place in Vossgard's final defense.
encounters.opening_view: Vossgard displays the march in absences. A closed road leaves one gate undermanned; a surviving command sounds from another. Engines, guides, prisoners, blood carts, surrendered companies, and exhausted battalions take only the places earned for them. Castellan Drenn shifts the living garrison around those facts while three breakout standards wait below the inner keep. Somewhere beyond the wall, a gate opens—or fails to. The first assault order will decide what the Compact abandons to reach Voss.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Vossgard is now a deployment board, not a riddle. Drenn's reinforcement marks, captured orders, and reports from the outer positions put the Bell gate, ridge postern, Underkeep Gate, garrison court, prisoner yards, and inner keep on one table. Merrow marks where engines can arrive; Dane marks surrendered troops, prisoners, and protected households; Holt and Vale mark the companies required to hold each open road.

The Compact already knows how to kill a vampire: sunlight mirrors, consecrated steel, stakes, fire, and soldiers drilled to use them. The difficulty is carrying those means to Voss while holding the walls, guarding prisoners, answering every force left in the rear, and closing the breakout road the Warrant left open.

The fortress takes the shape of the campaign that reached it. A preserved heavy route brings engines to the wall. Cooperative villages bring guides, food, and surrender channels. A bypassed command arrives as reinforcement or attacks the rear. Every closed exit consumes Compact troops; every open exit receives Voss's prisoners, blood, wagons, and surviving force.

## Command

Voss reads the same board from inside the keep. He commands the fortress and each surviving formation that can still answer through an open road. He prefers an organized breakout; if every military exit closes, he spends the living garrison and inner works to gain time for a sortie, last defense, or visible personal flight.

Castellan Lysa Drenn commands the living fortress garrison and household levies. Her loyalty belongs to the continuity of the Gloam March more than to Voss. A credible surrender record and visible separation of living levies from vampire cadres may bring her garrison to a stand-down.

Surviving encounter commanders appear according to campaign state:

- Arven Taal strengthens fortress engineering if he escaped the Causeway.
- Tal Vosca brings hostages and village levies if the villages were bypassed.
- Kasia Morcant provides mobile relief if the night riders survive.
- Halwen Rane and her knights defend the ridge and inner court if the Abbey remains active.
- Ossa Ren and the field reserve hold the bell gate if the Redoubt remains active.
- Ors Keln and the drowned force defend the lower gate if the Sluice remains active.

Return a commander only with the capability the Warrant allowed that command to preserve.

## The fortress on arrival

### Voss's concentration

The march-turn clock determines preparation:

- **Before turn four:** outer defenses are incomplete, many living troops remain distributed, and prisoners have not all been moved. The Compact arrives with less preparation of its own.
- **Turns four and five:** Vossgard has a coherent garrison, whatever stores or prisoners the announced turn-four reaction successfully moved, and at most the selected reinforcements that escaped their field positions. Other outer commands prepare, but none reaches the fortress merely because the clock advanced.
- **Turn six or later:** Voss has issued the general concentration and breakout order. Mobile bypassed forces can answer it; reduced forces cannot, and contained forces must break their named interdiction line before they can move.

### Army condition

- A **ready** army can conduct three major simultaneous tasks during the assault.
- A **strained** army can conduct two without direct intervention.
- A **spent** army can sustain one decisive main effort. Every other objective requires abandonment, local allies, or the Warrant’s direct intervention.

The tasks are:

1. breach and hold an approach;
2. screen bypassed forces and relief;
3. secure prisoner yards and prevent massacre or forced removal;
4. fix or separate the living garrison; and
5. pursue Voss into the inner keep.

### Military exits

- Red Abbey controlled or sufficiently contained: ridge road closed.
- Black Bell controlled or sufficiently contained: bell road closed.
- Drowned Sluice controlled or permanently blocked: canal exit closed.

With all three closed, Voss cannot organize a conventional breakout. With one open, he prepares a focused escape. With two or three open, he can feint at one route and move through another. Closed roads deny military movement, not every power Voss possesses. He may still abandon his army and attempt a visible escape by mist, climbing, or a dominated mount through the Compact's consecrated cordon. Such a flight becomes a pursuit through the line and carries no organized remnant, prisoners, blood, or stores.

## Choosing the final operation

### Rapid decapitation strike

Concentrate the army on the best available route and drive for the inner keep before Voss fully prepares. Early contact with him leaves prisoners, relief, and open exits with the least coverage.

### Full encirclement and assault

The Compact invests the fortress, assigns troops to all exits, and breaches through one or more controlled approaches. This converts prior reductions into a powerful final position but gives Voss time to prepare the inner defense and increases accumulated campaign cost.

### Living-garrison collapse

If the population is cooperative, surrender terms are credible, and **Enforceable terms can split the living levies from the dead** has been established, address Drenn and the levy companies before or during the assault. A stand-down removes living troops and may open a gate; Voss's dead and vampire cadres continue fighting.

### Forced sortie

If all exits are closed but the army is too spent for a full assault, the Compact threatens the blood stores, begins controlled bombardment, or demonstrates that no relief is coming. Voss may sortie to break the line. This brings him out of the keep at the cost of exposing the encircling troops to a concentrated attack.

### Limited siege and negotiated handover

Demand the surrender of the living garrison, prisoners, and fortress while offering Voss no safe conduct. The terms may isolate him and reduce casualties. The Ashen Gate and army condition put a hard cost on every hour of siege.

## The final operation

### Phase one: establish the breach

Select the ridge postern, bell gate, lower gate, a siege-train breach, or a costly improvised assault. Prior assets determine which routes exist and how many troops each consumes.

- The intact Iron Causeway and advanced siege train create a controlled wall breach.
- The Red Abbey creates a secure ridge approach.
- The Black Bell creates a central road approach and disrupts dead coordination.
- The Drowned Sluice creates a protected lower approach.
- A captured shadow-mount force can seize a gate before defenders fully redeploy.

### Phase two: answer the field consequences

Bypassed forces act openly. Night riders attack the rear, the Black Bell reserve advances, vampire knights counterattack, or causeway troops strike supply. The Compact must screen them, detach troops, or accept that they enter the fortress battle.

This phase collects the risks the Warrant knowingly purchased by bypassing field positions.

### Phase three: garrison court and prisoners

Drenn's living levies occupy the court while prisoners are gathered for movement or use as cover. Choose whether to assault through them, honor prior guarantees, attempt surrender under battlefield conditions, or assign another force to the yards.

Cooperative villagers, rescued prisoners, captured couriers, and prior surrender precedents turn a stand-down into an executable order addressed to actual companies, officers, and households.

### Phase four: inner keep

Voss retreats or counterattacks through the sunless hall, the officers' stair, and the coffin vault. He wins time by moving and recovering; the Warrant wins by keeping pressure on him.

If the blood reserve remains, Voss and surviving vampire troops recover between positions until access is physically denied. If it was destroyed, they fight on accumulated wounds. Consecrated assets provide the means; maintain pressure and close the escape.

### Phase five: settlement

Once Voss is destroyed, captured, or stopped during a personal flight, issue immediate orders:

- who commands the fortress overnight;
- how prisoners and surrendered troops are handled;
- whether local reeves form a provisional March council;
- whether the Compact occupies, protects, or evacuates the territory;
- what happens to collaborators promised hearings; and
- how much force remains while the rest returns through the Ashen Gate.

The Warrant's authority here is provisional. It can appoint overnight command, preserve records, assign custody, continue recorded protection and parole, and establish a temporary council from reeves, surviving civil clerks, road or canal officers, and surrendered commanders who have accepted review. It cannot settle permanent sovereignty or grant final amnesty; Rusk and the Compact's civil commission must review those questions at the next reliable contact.

Settlement begins before the blood dries. A spent army, opposed population, open roads, destroyed records, and intact enemy formations sharply limit which provisional orders can be enforced. An organized withdrawal must likewise name who protects or evacuates the population and how the fortress and crossing are denied to an immediate successor.

## Voss's behavior

Voss's decisions are governed by visible state.

- If two or more military exits remain open and the battle turns against him, he attempts an organized breakout with prisoners, blood, and the strongest surviving formation.
- If one exit remains open, he stages a major feint and commits his reserve to that route.
- If no exit remains open, he either launches a concentrated sortie, fights through the inner keep, or abandons the organized army for a visible personal flight through the cordon.
- If the living garrison remains loyal, he spends it to hold the court and walls.
- If the living garrison stands down, he relies on dead and vampire troops without gaining a replacement hidden force.
- If the blood reserve remains, he uses it to keep vampire units in action and sustain his own retreats.
- If the reserve is denied, he conserves vampire troops and seeks a shorter decisive engagement.

Show these intentions through deployments, signals, and orders. Once Voss commits a reserve, road, or prisoner column, that deployment fixes what the Compact can still intercept.

## Campaign assets in the finale

| Asset or condition | Concrete final effect |
| --- | --- |
| Intact Iron Causeway and siege train | Creates a controlled breach or suppresses a wall sector without spending the main effort. |
| Cooperative Tithe Villages | Provides guides, stretcher crews, food, intelligence on family levies, and a credible provisional government. |
| Reduced Thorn Barrows | Frees mobile troops to screen relief, chase a breakout, or shift between assault routes. |
| Reduced or contained Red Abbey | Closes the ridge exit; reduction also denies vampire recovery and provides a consecrated staging ground. |
| Reduced or contained Black Bell | Closes the bell road; reduction also disrupts coordinated dead formations and can misdirect surviving units. |
| Reduced or contained Drowned Sluice | Closes the canal exit; reduction also provides the lower assault and supply route. |
| Credible surrender record | Allows living officers to stand down without assuming summary execution or abandonment. |
| Ready army | Supports three simultaneous major tasks. |
| Strained army | Supports two simultaneous major tasks. |
| Spent army | Supports one major task; every other aim requires allies, sacrifice, or the Warrant’s intervention. |
| Stable Ashen Gate | Permits large casualty, prisoner, and civilian movement after victory. |
| Strained or imperiled Gate | Forces hard limits on evacuation and occupation. |

## Campaign outcomes

Use these outcomes to name the military and civil state left after the campaign.

### Decapitation

Voss is destroyed or captured, but major field forces, hostile population, or an unstable Gate prevent the Compact from holding the Gloam March. The Warrant can organize an evacuation or accept a dangerous occupation.

### Military victory

Voss is destroyed or captured, the organized field army is broken, the Ashen Gate survives, and the Compact controls the fortress long enough to choose an orderly withdrawal or occupation.

### Broken flight

Voss abandons his army and escapes alone or with a handful of attendants through the consecrated line. The invasion corridor, fortress, and organized field army are still broken, but the Warrant has failed its first war aim and leaves the Compact a continuing hunt, a political liability, and a ruler who may someday build another command.

### Durable victory

The military victory is joined to a cooperative or at least watchful population, functioning local administration, controlled roads, and enough army strength to protect the settlement. This need not mean direct Compact rule.

### Costly strategic failure

Voss escapes with a coherent force, or the Ashen Gate becomes unusable before the army and civilians can withdraw. The Warrant can still save thousands, destroy key enemy assets, or deny the immediate invasion corridor. Failure preserves the consequences of the campaign instead of resetting them.

reference_links.context: Rusk remains the reviewing campaign authority for final allocation, enforceable obligations, overnight command, and any later civil settlement.
Holt defines the Grey Banner infantry available for breach, containment, surrendered ground, and simultaneous final tasks.
Merrow defines what siege engines, engineers, repaired routes, and preserved infrastructure can actually support at the fortress.
Vale defines the mobile screen, courier interception, relief response, and pursuit capacity available around the final cordon.
Dane provides the standing machinery for garrison surrender, prisoners, protected civilians, requisition records, hearings, and provisional custody.
Voss commands the fortress and any organized remnant through the exits, formations, prisoners, stores, and blood the campaign left him.
Morcant matters at Vossgard only if her mobile command remains capable of relief, rear attack, or breakout support.
The Warrant remains bounded at the fortress: assault orders, surrender, prisoners, pursuit, and provisional administration each require real support and review.
The Gate remains the single road by which the final army is supplied and by which casualties, prisoners, civilians, records, and obligations return to daylight.
The Causeway defines whether heavy engines, bulk supply, and engineering capacity can reach the fortress approaches.
The villages define the grain, guides, levies, hostages, households, and surrender channels that may arrive at the fortress.
The Abbey defines the western postern, blood reserve, prisoner burden, cavalry approach, and protected ground available near the fortress.
The Bell defines the broad road and signal network by which a surviving field reserve can coordinate with the fortress.
The Sluice defines the eastern Underkeep route and the canal capacity available for supply, assault, or organized escape.
The Vossgard sheet preserves the known fortress geometry and outer-position relationships without deciding the final deployment or settlement.

revelations.title: The Iron Causeway can carry the heavy column intact
revelations.description: A two-part attack on the gatehouses and demolition galleries can save the span, break Krail’s grave cohort, and bring the siege train across the shadow plain.

revelations.title: The Tithe Villages can be secured before Voss empties them
revelations.description: A fast force can cut the crossroads, stop the hostage and grain columns, and give the villages terms strong enough to survive Voss’s reprisals.

revelations.title: The Thorn Barrows can carry a fast eastern advance
revelations.description: Displacing Morcant from the remount barrows and covered lanes opens the quickest route for cavalry, couriers, and light troops across the eastern March.

revelations.title: The Red Abbey can be cut off before it empties
revelations.description: Closing the ridge road and striking the cloister, prison yards, and blood vault denies Voss his knights, reserve blood, and northwestern exit.

revelations.title: The Black Bell can be struck before the field reserve withdraws
revelations.description: The tower, courier roads, command shelter, and mobile reserve can be broken or captured before they retire behind Vossgard’s walls.

revelations.title: The Drowned Sluice can be opened—or closed on Voss
revelations.description: Control of the Outer Chain, Sunken Turn, and Underkeep Gate creates a protected canal approach or denies the same route to an escaping court.

revelations.title: Three known roads can carry an assault into Vossgard
revelations.description: The ridge postern, Bell road, and Underkeep Gate each provide a workable entry. Each is also a conventional route Voss can use to break out.

revelations.title: A high-capacity route can bring the siege train to Vossgard
revelations.description: A stable Gate and either the intact Causeway or a working canal can carry the ram, sunlight mirrors, bulk ammunition, and sustained supply to the walls.

revelations.title: Enforceable terms can split the living levies from the dead
revelations.description: Named guarantees, protected families, functioning command channels, and visible restraint give living companies a practical way to stand down.

revelations.title: Closing three exits denies Voss an organized breakout
revelations.description: Holding the ridge road, Bell road, and Underkeep Gate—while preserving lateral mobility—forces Voss to fight inside the fortress or flee without an army.

revelations.title: Breaking the blood network weakens every vampire formation
revelations.description: Interrupting collection, convoy movement, storage, and final distribution denies Voss’s vampires the blood they need to recover through repeated fighting.

revelations.title: The Compact can hold the March after it wins
revelations.description: A stable Gate, controlled roads, working communications, local administration, and disciplined requisition can turn the conquered corridor into a defensible settlement.

clues.title: Merrow's two-team assault table
clues.description: Colonel Merrow’s assault table pairs a Gatewright gallery team with a formation assigned to fix the parapets. If both move before the defenders complete their next demolition drill, the span can be taken without accepting its destruction.
clues.discovery: Commit engineers and a covering formation at the opening council, or revise the table after defeating the bridgehead probe without spending those forces.

clues.title: The three-village removal window
clues.description: Reconnaissance reports place Voss’s carts at three different assembly points and show the removal columns cannot join until they reach the central crossroads. A fast column can block the junction before hostages and grain move south.
clues.discovery: Reconcile the scout reports at the command mound and assign enough troops or cavalry to exploit the timing.

clues.title: Vale's central-gap order
clues.description: Captain Vale identifies the central thorn gap as the only crossing Morcant cannot watch from two remount barrows at once. A supported advance there can force the night riders to reveal which station they will defend.
clues.discovery: Give Vale authority to screen the eastern axis and decide what infantry, scouts, or reserve will move behind her.

clues.title: The heavy-column manifest
clues.description: The manifest distinguishes loads that require reinforced road or barge from those pack animals can carry. Merrow can move the consecrated ram, sunlight mirrors, and bulk ammunition only if the Warrant preserves a high-capacity route and does not strand their crews at the Gate.
clues.discovery: Set the siege-train priority during the first council and inspect the loads whose movement determines later engineering options.

clues.title: The occupation board
clues.description: Rusk and Dane’s board names the replacement companies, hospital beds, interpreters, evacuation wagons, and civil officers available after the advance. It shows that the Compact can hold conquered ground only by preserving the Gate and assigning administration before every formation is committed forward.
clues.discovery: Establish surrender, requisition, and evacuation policy in the opening council, then leave a coherent reserve able to enforce it.

clues.title: Taal's western field-road bearings
clues.description: The bridge engineers’ bearings mark a maintenance descent onto the raised field roads north of Garren. Once the east gatehouse is controlled, a Compact column can enter the village crossroads behind Vosca’s removal screen instead of following the exposed main road.
clues.discovery: Seize the east gatehouse records, compel Taal’s cooperation, or preserve an engineer crew during the handover.

clues.title: The abbey convoy measure
clues.description: Captured axle marks and convoy orders show where the abbey road leaves the causeway and when its next blood and equipment train is expected. The junction can be occupied before Rane receives warning or uses the convoy as cover to withdraw.
clues.discovery: Take the dispatch station intact, question surrendered engineers, or compare the road wear with a captured convoy manifest.

clues.title: The reserve's crossing order
clues.description: A current order sends the Black Bell reserve across the causeway road in staggered cohorts before it turns south. A force moving from the bridge complex can reach the redoubt while its trenches and mobile reserve are divided.
clues.discovery: Capture the courier traffic during the causeway fight or obtain Taal’s authenticated copy of the reserve order.

clues.title: The load-bearing plates
clues.description: Plates in the demolition galleries mark which arches can bear the consecrated ram and where Gatewright braces must be placed. With the firing system disabled, the heavy column can cross without gambling the campaign on an untested span.
clues.discovery: Control the demolition galleries and preserve enough of the bridge mechanism for Merrow or Taal to inspect it.

clues.title: The west-road blood manifest
clues.description: The bridge dispatch office records sealed Red Abbey wagons by weight, escort, and destination. The schedule gives the road windows in which blood moves toward Vossgard and the escorts that must be intercepted or turned back.
clues.discovery: Capture the dispatch ledger, a convoy officer, or the authenticated cargo tallies before the garrison destroys them.

clues.title: Taal's bridge-service roster
clues.description: Taal's maintenance rolls name the engineers, stone crews, lifting specialists, and road wardens who kept the Causeway open before the war. Under recorded custody and work terms, the same cadre can maintain the Compact's only western heavy crossing and train replacements instead of disappearing into prison or Vossgard.
clues.discovery: Secure Taal's orderly room and accept the living engineers' surrender with named custody, work limits, and protection for their households.

clues.title: The shepherds' remount lanes
clues.description: Shepherds and field hands identify the covered lanes used to drive fodder and replacement coursers into the barrows. Their route reaches the rear of one remount station and avoids the gaps Morcant normally watches.
clues.discovery: Protect the households that know the route and secure their willing guidance rather than requisitioning it under threat.

clues.title: The abbey tithe road
clues.description: Stopped tithe carts and village teamsters reveal the abbey’s lower service road, its gate procedure, and the time required to move prisoners and blood uphill. A Compact column can cut the ridge before the depot completes its withdrawal.
clues.discovery: Stop a removal convoy, preserve its drivers, and obtain the reeves’ cooperation in identifying the road and expected traffic.

clues.title: Sila Marr's dry canal route
clues.description: Canal labor rolls and surviving workers identify a dry approach to the Outer Chain chamber and the crews needed to operate its counterweights. The route avoids the flooded road on which Keln expects a formal assault.
clues.discovery: Secure the labor records and protect Engineer Sila Marr or another canal crew willing to guide the Compact.

clues.title: The reeves' protection terms
clues.description: A witnessed agreement names how surrendered conscripts, accused collaborators, requisitioned stores, and Vossgard hostages will be treated. Copies carried forward give living soldiers something more credible than a battlefield promise.
clues.discovery: Reach enforceable terms with the reeves, stop reprisals and looting, and have Provost Dane issue the guarantees under Compact authority.

clues.title: The blood-tithe register
clues.description: The tithe house records collection days, household quotas, wagon capacities, and the officials who certify delivery. Break the network by freeing its people and denying the carts, not merely by burning one storehouse.
clues.discovery: Take the tithe house during the village operation or compel Vosca’s clerks to turn over the active collection books.

clues.title: The three-village duty roll
clues.description: The reeves’ shared roll names granary keepers, dike crews, teamsters, road watchers, and council messengers across Garren, Orra, and Lume. If the Compact preserves those offices rather than replacing every local function with soldiers, the villages can feed patrols, report movement, and form the first provisional civil authority after Voss falls.
clues.discovery: Protect the three councils, preserve their working records, and agree which local duties continue under Compact protection and later review.

clues.title: The reeves' refugee-road tally
clues.description: Years of hostage removals, tithe convoys, and emergency flights show that every mass movement from Vossgard reaches the northern March by the abbey ridge, the Bell road, or the canal. The lesser tracks can carry scouts or a fleeing vampire, but not wagons, prisoners, blood stores, and a coherent field formation.
clues.discovery: Compare the reeves’ movement tallies with current scout reports and obtain guides who can distinguish a military column from scattered personal flight.

clues.title: The covered western descent
clues.description: A rider lane descends from the western barrows to the causeway’s less-protected gatehouse and the shadow plain beneath it. Troops holding the barrow gap can place a gallery team there without advancing along the exposed road.
clues.discovery: Capture a remount station, force Morcant from the western lanes, or use seized shadow mounts to reconnoiter the descent under protection.

clues.title: Morcant's Bell-warning route
clues.description: Morcant’s dispatch route reaches the Black Bell tower through a narrow southern gap. Controlling the remounts or the gap lets the Compact strike the redoubt before riders can warn Ren or reinforce its courier screen.
clues.discovery: Break the rider rally system and follow the dispatch lane while the enemy is still reorganizing.

clues.title: The eastern towpath descent
clues.description: The southeastern barrow lane joins the old canal towpath above the flooded flats. A mobile force can descend directly on the Outer Chain chamber and avoid the drowned troops screening the lower road.
clues.discovery: Secure the southeastern lane and use rider maps, captured mounts, or Vale’s scouts to mark a route fit for the following force.

clues.title: Morcant's three-exit map
clues.description: The riders’ operational map shows how the ridge road, bell road, and canal exit connect beyond the fortress approaches. Holding the barrow lanes gives the Compact enough lateral mobility to reinforce whichever closure Voss tests.
clues.discovery: Capture Morcant’s command kit or reconstruct her response routes by controlling all three remount stations.

clues.title: Control of the march lanes
clues.description: With the remount stations reduced and the thorn gaps posted, couriers, patrols, and relief columns can move between the Gate, villages, and second belt without ceding every road to vampire cavalry.
clues.discovery: Leave a workable lane network, free the Dawn Lancers or captured mounts for patrol, and avoid collapsing every crossing in the fight.

clues.title: Morcant's recovery-cache circuit
clues.description: Morcant’s remount circuit includes sealed recovery caches timed to meet riders, abbey knights, and Bell couriers between operations. The cache tokens show that the blood network is not confined to the Red Abbey: mobile distribution lets wounded vampires return to action before a pursuing force expects them.
clues.discovery: Take a remount station intact, capture the cache tokens, or follow a wounded rider far enough to seize the next scheduled issue point.

clues.title: The repair-convoy seal
clues.description: The abbey’s engineer stores include authenticated seals and access instructions for repair crews admitted to the causeway galleries. Used promptly, they can place a Compact team inside the demolition system before Krail recognizes the substitution.
clues.discovery: Capture the depot office or accept the surrender of the living quartermaster staff before the seals and duty roster are destroyed.

clues.title: The canal depot records
clues.description: Blood shipments moved by canal during earlier campaigns, and the abbey retains lock-oil accounts, barge dimensions, and the current service order for the Underkeep Gate. The records turn preservation—or deliberate destruction—into a planned operation instead of a blind breach.
clues.discovery: Take the logistics office, preserve Voln’s staff, or recover the current canal packet from a departing convoy.

clues.title: The ridge-postern assault plan
clues.description: The captured ridge schedule identifies the postern guard, the wall section supported by abbey troops, and the ground on which a consecrated staging force can assemble beyond the fortress’s main missile arcs.
clues.discovery: Hold the ridge road and obtain the garrison rotation from prisoners, surrendered guards, or the abbey command office.

clues.title: The prisoners' garrison testimony
clues.description: Rescued prisoners and surrendered guards name which fortress companies are levies, where their families are held, and which officers have resisted feeding or reprisal orders. Compact guarantees can be addressed to actual units and households.
clues.discovery: Rescue the prison population and conduct an orderly surrender rather than allowing summary reprisals against the living garrison.

clues.title: The vault distribution board
clues.description: The vault board allocates preserved blood to Rane’s knights, the Black Bell lieutenants, and Vossgard’s inner keep by campaign turn. Capturing or destroying the depot at the correct point denies recovery to the formations most likely to oppose the final breach.
clues.discovery: Control the blood vault and its handling crews long enough to seize, spoil, or redirect the scheduled allotments.

clues.title: Voln's unfilled tithe-convoy board
clues.description: The abbey loading board assigns separate wagons, guards, and departure hours to Garren, Orra, and Lume. Empty columns and uncountersigned receipts show which removals have not yet reached the depot, allowing the Compact to cut the crossroads or intercept a specific convoy before people and grain disappear behind the ridge gate.
clues.discovery: Capture the logistics office, a departing convoy packet, or Voln’s current board before the staff burns the unfilled columns.

clues.title: Voln's stores-and-custody ledger
clues.description: Voln’s ledger names quartermasters, prison clerks, teamsters, well keepers, and ridge-road crews whose work outlasts the vampire depot. Preserved under hearing and supervision, that staff can distribute relief, maintain custody, and keep the western road functioning while the Compact builds a provisional administration.
clues.discovery: Take the outer abbey without destroying its offices, prevent reprisals against the living staff, and place their continuing duties under a named Compact or local officer.

clues.title: The village stand-fast order
clues.description: Ren’s current order tells Vosca when the field reserve can intervene and when the village levies must withdraw alone. Seizing the courier channel or sending a valid stand-fast tone can isolate the removal operation long enough for the Compact to secure the crossroads.
clues.discovery: Capture the current command packet, the courier staff, or the bell itself while the order remains operationally relevant.

clues.title: Rane's withdrawal sequence
clues.description: The signal schedule reserves a sequence for recalling the Red Abbey knights and clearing the ridge road. The Compact can strike before that sequence, falsify it, or block the road while the knights are committed elsewhere.
clues.discovery: Take Ren’s active signal slate or protect a captured bell crew long enough to identify and exploit the scheduled recall.

clues.title: The Bell-road gate packet
clues.description: The redoubt’s fortress packet assigns relief cohorts, gate watches, and fallback lines along the direct bell road. Once the reserve is broken or contained, the Compact has a mapped central approach and knows what force Voss expects to retreat through it.
clues.discovery: Capture the command shelter or obtain Ren’s authenticated fortress packet during surrender or pursuit.

clues.title: Ren's breakout contingency
clues.description: The reserve plan names the bell road as Voss’s principal overland breakout route and specifies how Ren’s cohorts will clear the gate, hold the road shoulders, and receive survivors from the other exits. Holding the redoubt and road denies the only route suited to a large organized withdrawal.
clues.discovery: Capture Ren’s active contingency packet, compel her staff to surrender it, or reconstruct the plan by seizing both the command shelter and the bell-road fallback positions.

clues.title: The March command network
clues.description: The bell relays, courier posts, ration stations, and surviving clerks form the only campaign-wide communication system already reaching every settlement and military road. Preserved under new authority, it can coordinate patrols and relief after the fortress falls.
clues.discovery: Take the redoubt without destroying all of its staff and relay infrastructure, then place it under an announced Compact or local command.

clues.title: Ren's canal-alarm sequence
clues.description: Ren’s signal slate reserves distinct tones for flooding the outer road, withdrawing the escape barges, and unweighting the Underkeep Gate. Capturing or falsifying the sequence lets a Compact column reach the lock chambers before Keln completes the response Voss expects.
clues.discovery: Seize the active signal slate, protect a bell crew able to read it, or control the tower long enough to test the canal tones against intercepted courier reports.

clues.title: Ren's living-company stand-down roster
clues.description: The reserve roster separates living companies from grave cohorts, names the officers who have objected to reprisals, and records which fortress households answer for their obedience. Addressed guarantees can divide Ren’s living reserve from Vark’s programmed dead before either force reaches Vossgard.
clues.discovery: Capture the command shelter or accept a disciplined surrender that preserves the roster, the living couriers, and the officers willing to carry authenticated terms forward.

clues.title: The recovery-tone allotment slate
clues.description: A bell-code slate pairs recovery tones with Red Abbey allotments, courier stations, and the vampire formations entitled to draw from them. The schedule lets the Compact intercept a mobile issue, send a false collection order, or identify which surviving unit will weaken first when the depot is denied.
clues.discovery: Take Ren’s current signal records and keep a clerk or bell crew alive long enough to match the coded tones to the allotment columns.

clues.title: The eastern towpath rise
clues.description: The outer lock survey marks where the towpath rises behind the southeastern barrows and which culverts remain passable to cavalry and light infantry. A force from the canal can enter the rider lanes behind Morcant’s normal screen.
clues.discovery: Control the Outer Chain chamber and send engineers or scouts along the exposed towpath before Keln floods or blocks it.

clues.title: The lower road beneath the Bell
clues.description: A lock-service road climbs from the Sunken Turn into the Black Bell’s resonance ditches below their prepared firing line. Troops can approach the tower from a direction Ren has assigned only courier guards to watch.
clues.discovery: Preserve the Sunken Turn controls and obtain Keln’s service map or Sila Marr’s operating route.

clues.title: The Underkeep Gate sequence
clues.description: The lock sequence fixes when the Underkeep Gate is unweighted, where its drowned guard must stand, and how barges can deliver an assault force beneath the outer wall. The route is dangerous and workable with controlled mechanisms.
clues.discovery: Take the three lock mechanisms intact or compel the lock crews to demonstrate the fortress opening sequence.

clues.title: The verified lock-depth table
clues.description: Gatewright soundings mark which engines can be broken into barge loads, where tow teams can work under cover, and how much bulk supply reaches the fortress per cycle. An open canal can replace a destroyed causeway as the campaign’s heavy route.
clues.discovery: Control the locks long enough for engineers to sound the canal and preserve the barges, towpath, and lifting gear.

clues.title: The escape-barge orders
clues.description: Keln’s withdrawal orders assign barges, guards, and loading priority for Voss’s lower-gate breakout. Capturing the craft and closing the Underkeep Gate removes the last route by which an organized remnant can leave the fortress unseen from the walls.
clues.discovery: Seize the barge station or the lock marshal’s active orders before the boats withdraw beneath Vossgard.

clues.title: Marr's canal-ward roll
clues.description: Marr’s roll links lock crews, levee wardens, barge masters, towpath gangs, and the low-ground households each mechanism protects. Preserving that network gives the postwar March transport, flood control, and a civilian chain of responsibility that soldiers cannot improvise from an occupied gatehouse.
clues.discovery: Secure the operating records, protect the living crews from Keln and reprisals, and assign a named authority to continue canal work under review.

clues.title: Drenn's fortress levy rolls
clues.description: The garrison court rolls place living companies beside the households Voss holds and identify the officers Castellan Drenn believes will stand down under enforceable protection. The rolls let the Compact split the court before the inner keep fight consumes it.
clues.discovery: Reach the garrison court, capture its orders, or negotiate directly with Drenn and the levy officers under cover of earlier guarantees.

clues.title: Drenn's gate-reinforcement board
clues.description: Drenn’s board places the ridge postern, Bell gate, and Underkeep Gate beside their reinforcement times, interior stairs, and fallback courts. A first investment can therefore convert one captured approach into a plan for a later return without pretending that the other two routes were inaccessible or unknown.
clues.discovery: Hold an outer work, capture a garrison command post, or negotiate access to Drenn’s current reinforcement board before the fortress staff relocates it.

clues.title: The freight-yard receiving marks
clues.description: Painted receiving marks in the western freight yard and lower hoist chamber match the ram sections, mirror frames, ammunition wagons, and barge loads on Merrow’s manifest. They confirm where a preserved Causeway or opened canal can deliver the heavy train directly into a controlled assault sector.
clues.discovery: Reach the western yard or lower works with Gatewrights, captured engineers, or the heavy-column manifest and compare the surviving hoists and gate clearances.

clues.title: Voss's breakout loading table
clues.description: Voss’s loading table assigns prisoners, blood, officers, wagons, and surviving formations to the ridge road, Bell road, and canal according to which remain open. No fourth line can carry an organized remnant; the margin separately records mounts and mist screens for Voss’s personal flight.
clues.discovery: Capture a fortress operations room, a breakout courier, or the loading staff while the assignments still correspond to visible deployments.

clues.title: The inner-keep blood-service table
clues.description: The service table times blood from the lower vaults to the Bell gate, ridge court, vampire reserve, and Voss’s own retreat chambers. It identifies the physical handoff points where denying carriers or cistern access prevents several wounded formations from recovering between phases of the assault.
clues.discovery: Seize a service stair, blood carrier, or inner-court order station before the schedule is abandoned during the final withdrawal.

clues.title: The civil-continuity docket
clues.description: The fortress docket names surviving civil clerks, road and canal officers, grain custodians, hearing dates, and the local orders that must be renewed before dawn. It gives the Warrant a bounded provisional administration instead of asking exhausted battalions to invent government after the battle.
clues.discovery: Preserve the garrison court and records during the assault, then place the named offices under temporary command, custody, and civil review rather than treating every servant of Voss as an enemy formation.
